content:
Hi all,

Just to make sure we sync, I will soon start working on world satisfaction to get to the invariants.
I think with recently merged BI for bigOpM we should have enough pieces. I'll ping in this thread, when there's an update on that.
@Sergei Stepanenko We had very similar plans/hopes with @Fernando LEAL -- let's make sure to coordinate :)

ralfj said:

Sergei Stepanenko We had very similar plans/hopes with Fernando LEAL -- let's make sure to coordinate :)

Definitely! :)

It would be nice to have the whole invariant part to start working on the program logic part.

I've made a draft PR (https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean/pull/303). I don't expect this PR to change much functionally, but there's still some refactoring left, so some renamings can happen.

Also, now src/Iris/Instances/Lib/WSat.lean can serve as an example for how to do the preGS/GS ghost state definition from Rocq. I tweaked it so that no annotations were needed on the top-level theorems, just {GF : BundledGFunctors} and [W : WsatGS GF] in the context. GNames are accessed via W, so if you drop down to the iOwn level you still need to explicitly supply the ElemG fields like (E := W.inv). But I think in client code, those extra annotations should now be absent.

Thank you! And sorry for the typeclass mess. I was not sure what is the intended way to do it, when writing the port.
Don't apologize, I didn't know either! I don't think anyone had defined a resource algebra composition in the full Iris pattern yet. I was noting this here as an example for how to do it.

Just a small update before the end of the week:

The remaining parts until we get to the invariants: later credits (LC) -> fancy updates (model) -> invariants.
I'm almost done with the mechanical part of porting later credits, but will probably take some time with integrating it, because I would like to think more about ways to allow both for LC Iris and non-LC Iris.

I think ETA for the draft PR is ~middle/end of the next working week, so we could discuss it on Friday.

I'm not sure if it was discussed before, but is the plan to preserve LC/non-LC choice? IIRC, LC invalidate only some rules, which are not really used in practice, and in the Rocq version the choice is motivated mostly by backwards compatibility, which is not a problem for the Lean implementation.

Sergei Stepanenko said:

I'm not sure if it was discussed before, but is the plan to preserve LC/non-LC choice? IIRC, LC invalidate only some rules, which are not really used in practice, and in the Rocq version the choice is motivated mostly by backwards compatibility, which is not a problem for the Lean implementation.

If you have a chance, you should ask Amin Timany about this. IIRC he has use cases for the non-LC version. When you search the Iris Helpdesk for later credits, you find a bunch of things people want to do that only work with later credits disabled. See for example the discussion here or here.
I needed the non-LC in the adequacy proof for DimSum. It might be possible that I can use the LC version there if I use excluded middle, but I am not fully sure. But I don't think that the non-LC version is only used by legacy code, also new developments might need it, so I think it would be good to have an option to use the non-LC version.

Thanks for the links! Hm, interesting, the first example seem to imply that in classical Lean setting it should work with later credits. I'm curious now, if BiFUpdSbi can be constructed for the LC version with LEM.
I'll talk with Amin on Monday and write a summary here, and implement both versions.

Sergei Stepanenko said:

I'm curious now, if BiFUpdSbi can be constructed for the LC version with LEM.

My intuition is that one can construct BiFUpdSbi using LEM if one restricts to pure propositions, but it does not work if one wants to extend it to plain propositions. (In fact, I am not sure what LEM on plain propositions would mean.) But as you say I think it is best to talk with Amin about this.

The draft PR is here: https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean/pull/314
It implements later credits, model of fancy updates, and invariants along with some minor things that were missing for that.

There's still a lot of work on refactoring, so probably merging it might take some time.
In particular, I will make a few passes of going over the proofs, and making them less messy, and marking rocq names.

At the very end, there're two versions of fancy updates: with and without later credits. Seems like there's no way of escaping it.

I've skipped PM instances related to framing and invariants. Probably, we should open an issue for them until this functionality is implemented for the PM.

This is really cool! I looked into some of the proof mode problems you ran into and found two issues, which I fixed in https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean/pull/318 and https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean/pull/319. In particular with these changes, you should be able to get rid of the (GF := GF) annotations and solve the FIXME about iapply IH.
Thanks for looking into it, that exactly solves the problem! I think it will also help with refactoring WSat.
